Use a one-dimensional dynamic-programming array, initially zero. For each item, process capacities downward from capacity to its weight, choosing the better of skipping it or adding its value to the best result at the remaining capacity. The invariant is that after processing each item, dp[c] is the maximum value attainable using only processed items with total weight at most c. Descending updates ensure the remaining-capacity state still excludes the current item, preventing reuse.

Empty inputs or zero capacity return zero; overweight items are skipped, zero-value items cannot improve the result, and an exact-fit item is eligible.
